name: Profile
grades: A: no errors and at most 1 warning. B: no errors. C: 1 error. D: 2 errors. F: 3 or more. Each rule counts once, however many places it fires. Hints never count.

2.name: Name or handle as a heading in the page

3.name: List or grid of what the person made, posted or sold

5.name: Icons at the top right (gear, share, more)

9.name: Follow, add or edit button near the name

10.name: Banner or cover picture behind the avatar

v1.name: Creator or social profile
expect: An avatar near the top, with the name set as a heading close to it
A back control at the top left
Gear, share or more icons at the top right
A list or grid of the person's posts below the header

v2.name: Own account profile
expect: An avatar at the top, with the name beside or under it
A gear or other icon at the top right
The bottom tab bar still in view
The person's own posts or items below the header

v3.name: Seller or business page
expect: A back control at the top left
A name with an avatar or logo near the top
A row of ratings or other counts that help a stranger decide

v4.name: Sheet or card profile
v4.lead: Profile as a sheet or card
expect: A close control or a Done button at the top
No bottom tab bar, because the card sits over another screen

not_checked: What happens after a tap on Follow, Edit or the top right icons: one screen cannot show it.
Whether the tabs switch the list below and whether the list loads more as it scrolls.
A profile with nothing posted yet: that is a second state, and only the state on the screen is graded.
The name heading's contrast and size are left out of the checks: on a few screens the handle itself carries the name of the screen source, which the report cannot print.

rules.says: A long bio with no name heading and no photo, so the reader cannot tell who it is about.
rules.why: The sheet shows a long bio but neither the person's name nor a photo, so the reader cannot tell who it is without reading the text. Seen on 1 of 54 checked screens.

rules.says: A toast banner sits over the top of the page and covers the avatar or the name.
rules.why: A toast banner covers the top of the page: it cuts across the avatar on Hypelist and the header on HEY. Seen on 3 of 54 checked screens.

rules.says: The counts are set in small grey text over a photo and are hard to read.
rules.why: The stats are set in small grey text over a photo and are hard to read. Seen on 2 of 54 checked screens.

rules.says: Text or a close control is too faint against what is behind it.
rules.why: Accessibility guidelines ask for 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text: 18 pt, or 14 pt bold (button labels are bold). Controls, such as a close or back glyph, need 3:1. Below 3:1 is an error; from 3:1 to 4.5:1 on smaller text it is a warning. Checked on the labels of buttons, the lines of the parts marked as key text, and the close and back glyphs. Not checked on a dimmed screen or over a photo or a pattern, or on the label of a greyed-out button (the guidelines leave out controls that cannot be used yet). Faint placeholder text in an empty field is only a hint, since iOS's own placeholder grey is about 1.7:1.

rules.says: Text is smaller than 11 pt.
rules.why: Apple lists 11 pt as the smallest text size on iOS. Measured from the height of each line, so it is about right, not exact. Checked on the parts marked as key text.

rules.says: A control sits under the status bar or the home indicator.
rules.why: The status bar row at the top and the bottom 34 pt, where the home indicator sits, belong to the system on phones without a home button. Flagged when a control reaches the status bar row or comes within 17 pt of the bottom edge, so a button that only touches the area is not counted.

rules.says: A close or back control is drawn smaller than 13 pt.
rules.why: Apple asks for a 44 x 44 pt tap area. The standard close X in a bar is drawn about 13 to 17 pt across inside that area, so only a smaller drawing is flagged. A screenshot cannot show the tap area itself, so this is a hint.
